content.title: Anthropic researcher claims to have proven Riemann hypothesis using Claude
content.summary: An Anthropic PBC researcher, Levent Alpöge, announced on his personal website that he used the AI model Claude to produce a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a long‑standing open problem in mathematics. The claim follows Anthropic’s recent Nasdaq listing that raised over $93 billion, but the company has not issued an official statement and the alleged proof, spanning more than 250,000 pages, remains unpublished.

content.title: Three insights you may have missed from theCUBE’s coverage of the Dell Technologies New York Symposium
content.summary: The Dell Technologies New York Symposium highlighted that enterprise AI requires a new operating and economic model, with the focus shifting from tools and models to the specialized knowledge embedded in AI systems. The event also emphasized that AI infrastructure decisions must consider more than compute capacity, evaluating performance, data control, and cost across cloud, data center, and edge environments.

content.title: Inference now drives two-thirds of AI workloads, changing where chips get deployed
content.summary: Inference now accounts for about two-thirds of AI workloads, shifting infrastructure focus from large training clusters to smaller, modular data centers that prioritize power, cooling, and memory supply. Positron AI Inc., which raised $875 million at a $5 billion valuation, builds inference appliances using commodity memory and plans to tape out its own silicon for its Titan server, while Oracle Corp. is deploying 340 Atlas servers in its cloud.

content.title: Sovereign AI: Where control becomes an architectural requirement
content.summary: The article discusses the growing need for sovereign AI, emphasizing that organizations must control the systems that generate intelligence, especially in regulated industries. It highlights gaps in current vendor claims, the cost of adding isolated environments, and AWS's low score due to lack of customer‑run air‑gapped stacks, underscoring the trade‑off between local jurisdiction risk and model capability.

content.title: AI claimed a solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis — and a human did, too
content.summary: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, announced a Lean‑compilable solution to the Riemann hypothesis while his employer became the first publicly traded frontier AI lab. He also released a proof of the Navier–Stokes equations with NYU mathematician Tristan Buckmaster, and the community is debating the role of AI, with Alpöge describing how Claude helped him find the argument.

content.title: Daniel Ek backs AI researcher’s fusion power startup. Here’s what they’re building.
content.summary: Spotify founder Daniel Ek has backed Europa Fusion, a stealth fusion power startup founded by AI researcher Nantas Nardelli, who previously worked at Google DeepMind, Facebook AI Research, and Microsoft Research Cambridge. Nardelli, who was head of machine learning at Pacific Fusion, believes fusion startups should focus on simulation and data rather than hardware, and Europa Fusion will pursue a pulsed‑power approach to fusion.

content.title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
content.summary: The article lists several AI agents that can be accessed via text messaging, including Instinct, Ask Proxy, Caddy, Folk, Haven, Poke, and Underdog, each offering features such as scheduling, context memory, and device‑side privacy. It also notes funding milestones and platform approvals, such as Instinct’s $10 billion valuation, Poke’s Apple Messages for Business approval, and Underdog’s on‑device model.

content.title: Is selling an AI version of your face to this microdrama startup the future of Hollywood?
content.summary: Shortical, a microdrama startup founded last January, has begun producing AI-generated content to reduce production costs, featuring a wholly AI series called “Inevitable” that uses a digital avatar of actor Aki Avni. The company promotes a “LICENSE YOUR FACE” program, inviting public figures to submit their social media handles for potential contracts to license their personas in its AI-generated dramas.

content.title: Hours after Anthropic claims a Claude proof of the Riemann hypothesis, Stanford releases an all-human competing draft
content.summary: Anthropic's mathematician Levent Alpöge and the AI model Claude presented a Lean-verified proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, while Stanford researchers released an entirely human proof by Alessandro Masullo within hours. Both proofs are under scrutiny, with the AI proof backed by computer verification and the human proof vetted by Stanford mathematician Brian Conrad.

content.title: Nvidia researchers argue huge AI context windows are a dead end
content.summary: Nvidia researchers argue that extremely large context windows for language models are unnecessary and costly, noting that periodic summaries and targeted lookups performed comparably to processing entire novels. They highlight GPT‑4’s 8,192‑token window and GPT 5.6 Sol’s one‑million‑token window, concluding that handling whole books is overkill.

content.title: OpenAI shares new prompting tips for GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol to fix brief answers and unnecessary questions
content.summary: OpenAI released new prompting templates for its GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol models, advising developers to update system prompts to reduce brief answers and unnecessary questions. The updates also include coding guidelines that encourage reuse of existing code, limit abstractions, and add tests only when requested, while the Responses API now discards earlier reasoning content when conversation history is edited or the model is switched.

content.title: Silicon Valley's growing obsession with AI doomsday is turning parts of the tech industry toward cult-like devotion
content.summary: The article reports that a Vermont organization called Maple recruits tech workers and claims to build an AI god modeled on its leader Soryu Forall's mind, while former members allege systematic manipulation and surveillance. It also notes that OpenAI investors have made claims about shadow networks, Anthropic retired a Claude model in 2025, and a 2024 AI Impacts survey found an 18% average chance of AI causing human extinction.

content.title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
content.summary: Anthropic's IPO has sparked debate over whether the company can maintain its safety-first mission while satisfying shareholders, as the AI lab becomes the first to go public. Meanwhile, Microsoft plans to reduce token costs and make AI vendors interchangeable, prompting businesses to evaluate models for efficiency, while Anthropic faces pressure to release frontier models quickly amid Nvidia's $10 billion investment.

content.title: The Outages Are Just Getting Started
content.summary: The article discusses a series of recent outages affecting major tech firms and institutions, attributing many to routine failures exacerbated by rapid AI‑driven vulnerability discovery and patching pressures. It highlights that while no coordinated AI attacks were confirmed, the speed of AI tools is straining systems and accelerating the need for immediate patch deployment.

content.title: Cops Are Pushing Extremely Corny ‘Grand Theft Auto 6’ Slop
content.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI was released after a 13‑year wait, and police departments across the U.S. and Canada have used AI‑generated images and Instagram posts to promote recruitment and public messaging, often mimicking the game's aesthetic. The posts range from playful slogans like “Join San Diego PD VI” to warnings about real‑world law enforcement, reflecting a mix of marketing and cautionary content.

content.title: Jensen Huang’s ‘Lying’ Alarmed Nvidia Board Ahead of His Resignation
content.summary: Nvidia's board ousted CEO Jensen Huang after allegations of extramarital affairs and repeated lying, citing integrity and trust concerns. The decision followed an independent investigation into potential foreign intelligence involvement and was publicly confirmed during an all‑hands meeting on November 18.
